analysis.title: DeskTalk - Markets drop, chop and stabilize
key_insights: Sharp intraday moves at the NY mid-morning: IPO and single-stock noise weighed on tech, while weakness across EMFX and gold points to broader de-risking. Conviction is limited, with tentative signs of stabilization into the European close.
Citi's D1 desk says its IPO Funding basket (CGUSAFND Index) is up 2% vs Nasdaq up 0.3%. Investors are selling AI winners to fund new issuance, with AMD headlines adding noise.
AMD and Nasdaq are stabilizing, with Nasdaq finding support toward 27,000. Semis are the most active sector on the cash desk. Citi's Cybersecurity basket (CGTSCYBR Index) is up 5% intraday.
Gold (XAU) is down 1.2%, weighing on the commodity complex and ZAR, which is again among the worst performers. The sales desk says ownership has stayed sticky through recent gold selloffs.
The sales desk says gold ETF holdings could become a meaningful source of supply if broader risk assets come under pressure. Clients are expressing this risk via knock-out structures.

The FX trader sees no obvious reason for the USD retracement and calls it a very low conviction market. The eTrading desk notes elevated FX volumes, with USDCNH interbank volumes about 500% above historical averages.

USDBRL is up 0.6% after a brief knee-jerk move following BCB intervention. Liquidity is thin ahead of a local holiday tomorrow, and the trader expects the intervention to stabilize price action for now.
Rates are unable to rally despite risk-off sentiment. Oil is about 1% higher on geopolitical headlines.
Axios reported that President Trump is still considering a joint attack with Israel, but strikes are not imminent. Iran's IRGC said there would be no nuclear talks until Hormuz is settled.
